title: Declare what a function returns
objective: Use returns to say what kind of value a function gives back, and read a function's result as a value.

body.text: A returns line tells the reader and the compiler what kind of value the function gives back. Write returns a number, returns text, or returns a boolean. The value after gives back must match that kind. A function with a returns line can be used anywhere a value of that kind is expected, such as in a say line.

body.title: Adding and greeting
body.code:
function add
    takes number called left
    takes number called right
    returns a number
    gives back left plus right

say add 3 and 4

function greeting
    takes text called name
    returns text
    gives back "Hello, {name}!"

say greeting "Ada"

body.text: A function can return a boolean, which is true or false. This is useful for a yes-or-no check. The function below returns the answer to score is at least 0, so a negative score gives false.

body.title: A yes or no answer
body.code:
function valid
    takes number called score
    returns a boolean
    gives back score is at least 0

say valid -1
say valid 5

body.prompt: double should return twice its input, but it adds 2 instead. Change it so double 5 prints 10.
body.starter:
function double
    takes number called value
    returns a number
    gives back value plus 2

say double 5
body.solution:
function double
    takes number called value
    returns a number
    gives back value times 2

say double 5
